The provided evidence (Source [S1]) explicitly introduces 'GES (Generalized Exponential Splatting)' as a novel representation in the abstract and body, describing it as a method that replaces Gaussian basis functions with Generalized Exponential Functions (GEF) to improve efficiency and rendering quality. The content matches the description of the paper cited in the claim.

The claim matches this specific statement found in the evidence.

1.  **Mean Position** ($\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$): 3D vector $(x, y, z)$ [S1].

The evidence explicitly defines the Generalized Exponential Function (GEF) used in the GES method. Specifically, the text states: 'where µ ∈ R is the location parameter' and provides the formula involving $|x - µ|$. In the context of 3D scene representation (as opposed to 1D signal fitting), the location parameter µ corresponds to the 3D position vector $(x, y, z)$. The evidence confirms that µ is a learnable parameter representing the location/mean of the splat.
supported
